summary: Read an item using a positive or negative position.
documentation: at returns the item at a zero-based index. Negative indices count backward from the end, so -1 selects the final item. An index outside the array yields undefined rather than wrapping around.
inputs: An integer position, interpreted relative to array length when negative.
returns: The selected item, or undefined when out of range.
caution: Use an explicit missing-value policy when returning JSON: undefined cannot be represented as a normal JSON value.
scenarios: Show the latest recorded stock movement.
Read the final status in an order history.
Compare a recent sensor reading with the previous one.
title: Read the most recent event
problem: Input is an array of JSON event objects. Return the final object, or null when there are no events. Preserve all fields on the returned object.
goal: Use Array.at() or an equivalent approach demonstrating the same premise.
hint: Use index -1 and handle the empty array explicitly.
